Leaders of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) on Wednesday condemned an article published in ‘Sakshi’ Telugu daily against their party president Y.S. Sharmila, alleging that it contained derogatory remarks that undermined the dignity of women.
They demanded an unconditional public apology from the newspaper, and urged the Press Council of India to take appropriate action.
As part of a demonstration staged at the party office, Andhra Ratna Bhavan, they burnt copies of the newspaper.
Leading the protest, APCC vice-president Kolanukonda Shivaji accused the newspaper of resorting to character assassination through fabricated and unverified reports. He alleged that it was an attempt to portray Ms. Sharmila extending a wedding invitation to the Chief Minister as an objectionable act and reflected the “low standards of journalism being practised by the newspaper.”
Mr. Shivaji demanded that the Editors Guild intervene and ensure that the Sakshi management and its owners issue a public apology to Ms. Sharmila. He said the issue was not merely an insult to an individual woman, but reflected a broader attitude of disrespect towards women and their dignity.
Questioning the priorities of the publication, Mr. Shivaji said while the State was grappling with several important issues, including the cyclone situation, El Niño, electoral roll revision under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and concerns relating to the Election Commission, the newspaper chose to target Ms. Sharmila over a routine social gesture.
